candidate.answerReason: The integer solutions are -2, -1, 0, 4, 5, and 6, whose sum is 12.

methods.label: Find the allowed integer squares
methods.explanation:
Because \(x\) is an integer, \(x-2\) is also an integer. Its square is strictly between \(1\) and \(25\) exactly when
\[x-2=\pm2,\ \pm3,\ \pm4.\]
These possibilities are exhaustive: magnitudes \(0\) and \(1\) give squares at most \(1\), while magnitudes at least \(5\) give squares at least \(25\).

Adding \(2\) gives the six distinct solutions
\[-2,\ -1,\ 0,\ 4,\ 5,\ 6.\]
Pairing values equally far from \(2\), their sum is
\[(-2+6)+(-1+5)+(0+4)=12.\]
The answer is \(\boxed{12}\), choice B.
